The petitioner has challenged the prosecution initiated against her in PCR.No.6334/2015 before the XLIV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru and the consequent order dated 24.02.2016 taking cognizance of the offence punishable under Sections 23, 24, 25, 108, 109, 191,
192, 415, 420, 463 and 464 of IPC and registering C.C.No.5043/2016.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts that can be discerned from the private complaint and put in a nutshell are that the respondent No.2 claimed that a property was purchased by his brother and that he had raised a housing loan to construct a building thereon.
She claimed that her brother lost his employment and was therefore, unable to pay the monthly EMI's.
Consequently, he offered to help his brother to pay the EMI's.
Thus, out of natural love and affection, her brother executed a gift deed in her favour.

She claimed that the accused No.1 is her sister-in- law and that she was representing to the general public that the property belonged to her husband and herself and that she was attempting to encumber the same in more ways than one, which prompted the respondent No.2 to lodge a private complaint.

The trial Court took cognizance of the offences and issued process which is challenged in the present petition by the accused No.1.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had filed Crl.Misc.No.397/2011 under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and that in order to overcome the fallout of the said proceedings, the gift deed dated 20.07.2011 was fraudulently executed.

Later the petitioner filed a suit in O.S.No.7005/2012 for a declaration that she is entitled to remain in possession of the property for partition and separate possession of her share in the suit schedule property and that the issues raised by the respondent No.1 in the private complaint are also the subject matter of the suit in O.S.No.7005/2012.
He therefore contends that the prosecution of the petitioner may be set at naught pending disposal of the civil suit in O.S.No.7005/2012.
He further contends that a petition in M.C.No.4482/2013 was filed by the husband of petitioner under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1956.

She therefore submits that the instant private complaint is nothing but an abuse of process of law and Courts and the trial Court without noticing that it is purely a civil dispute has taken cognizance.
4.

Learned counsel for the respondent No.2 on the other hand submitted that the brother of the respondent No.2 had lawfully executed a gift deed and therefore, the petitioner had no subsisting right, title or interest therein.
He contended that the petitioner cannot even contest the right of the brother of the respondent No.2 to execute the gift deed.

He submitted that the petitioner is now attempting to represent to the general public that the property in question is available for rent and thereby is attempting to create third party interest, thus, affecting the right, title and interest of the Jayanthi vs The State

By J.P.Nagar Police Station on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148214568/
2 respondent No.2 in the property in question.
5.

If the parties are litigating over the very same property in a Civil Court, the respondent No.2 cannot strong- arm the petitioner by filing a private complaint urging the same questions which are seized before the Civil Court in O.S.No.7005/2012.
It is evident from the records that the respondent No.2 has attempted to give the case a criminal twist to prosecute the petitioner, which is impermissible.
6. In that view of the matter, this petition is allowed.

The prosecution of the petitioner in PCR.No.6334/2015 pending trial before the XLIV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bengaluru and the order dated 24.02.2016 taking cognizance of the offences punishable under Sections 23, 24, 25, 108, 109, 191, 192, 415, 420, 463 and 464 of IPC is quashed.
